It was most perplexing that all my searching found no solution, only more people with the same problem with their Moto G7. I have been a Moto G phone user for years and relied on CNET reviews of the phone which was always their favorite of the budget phones. I owned a Moto G4 initially and loved it so much I upgraded to a Moto G5 when it came out. Right now I am so glad that I kept that Moto G5 because I have put the SIM card back in it and that is my lifeline while I see what will have to be one with my newer G7. The Moto G5 is making calls and working just fine. For anyone interested, I will update this review once I have dealt with Motorola Customer Support.

G7 is a downgrade from the G6. This was to replaced my beloved moto G6, but is a downgrade from the G6, it lags, it feels slow, horrible camera, washout screen, low resolution, I am having a much pleasant experience with the Samsung A20 which is better in every way. This G7 was from India and to be honest didn’t work very well with cricket, it recognized the SIM card immediately, I was impressed by that, but the cell signal was always weak and very often I would loose data connection at places where I would normally be okay with other phones, Cricket has very good cell coverage, so I will blame it on this phone. I would not recommended it. The G6 was a true revelation for its time, but the G7 really disappointed.

The unlocked Motorola Moto G7 is just an amazing phone.. I've had the Moto G7 for a little over 2 weeks now. So far it is an amazing upgrade from the Moto G6. The performance from the G7 is a great upgrade from the G6. But the design is not. The Moto G7 design is just a bigger version of the G6. It also does not have NFC. Not having NFC or a updated design is the only things about the Moto G7 I don't like. I love having 64GB of storage and an SD card slot that allows up to a 128GB card. With the snapdragon 632 processor and 4GB RAM this Moto G7 runs great. Also you can play some games on this phone. On the G7 I can play the Call of Duty Mobile game just fine on medium graphics and high frame rate. The battery is good at 3000MAH.

The Moto G6 has a 5.7 size screen compared to the Moto G7 6.2, so the bigger the screen, the more battery will be in use. Motorola decided to give the G7 the same 3,000mAh battery capacity as the G6 and relies on the Android Pie's Adaptive Battery feature instead of increasing the Moto G7 battery capacity to atleast 3500mAh. The Moto G7 CPU is more power efficient than the Moto G6, but not enough to offset the smaller battery for it's screen size. Compared to the Moto G7 Play and Power, Motorola decided to remove Band 71 which is a great band for T-Mobile users in rural areas and is going to be a band that T-Mobile is going to use more of. It makes no sense to have Motorola's "lesser" G7 Play and Power to have this band and not the higher spec G7.

Don't waste your money!. I am so burned out on Apple products. I decided to get rid of my iphone and try out an android cell phone for the first time. I decided to try the Moto G7 Power. While the G7 has a 3000 mAh battery, the G7 Power has a 5000 mAh battery!

I chose the Moto G7 based on my previous satisfactory experience with Moto G phones and the reviews which said it was one of the best budget smartphones in US market. I was thoroughly disappointed - not only comparing the G7 to the Asus but even to the previous Moto G phones. Here are my impressions of the Moto G7 after using it for about 1 month as my only and main phone. Display - Washed out, lacking in brightness and saturation. The Asus was way better in terms of brightness, color, accuracy, sharpness. Sound - Bad. The speaker is too loud and harsh for itself. At full volume the sound cracks. No wonder there are so many complaints of the speakers going out after a few days of use - did Motorola even test them thoroughly ? Does not seem so.

Photos with the Moto G7 are okay, but seem to lack the snap that older phone's photos had. Otherwise, the Moto G7 has worked well for me. The phone sounds excellent, watching YouTube videos on the big 6.2-inch screen is good (and there is plenty of volume in a quiet room), and it is great for texting, music playing and all the typical stuff. One thing that really surprised me about the Moto G7 was that it does not have a standard micro-USB port for charging and data exchange -- it has a USB-C port. This really caught me by surprise, and I still am somewhat disappointed that it does not have a micro-USB port, since I have micro-USB cables and chargers everywhere.

The only downside to my usage so far is the selfie camera, it could be much better. Other than that, sarisfied.

04_strip_model.text: In good lighting the pictures look great, however shadows can stick out quite pathologically. Overall I am very satisfied with the product, keeping in mind that the weaknesses mentioned above are an acceptable sacrifice in quality for the cost of the phone. If you are trying to take near-professional quality images with a phone, this is not the product for you. Other than image acquisition and a mediocre (but acceptable) battery life, you likely won't notice any performance differences from higher-end phones.

Not impressed. I bought this phone for the excellent camera reviews. The camera was terrible. Literally couldn’t take a clear picture no matter how still I held it. Text messages often didn’t deliver (and this was to other Android users - so not an iPhone issue). Also glitchy from the moment I bought it, with apps closing me out for no reason and freezing up. I returned the phone. Only gave it more than one star because I mean... it worked. Just didn’t work well.

The camera does need to be learned in order to avoid its weaknesses, since it's obviously not a flagship phone. Digital zoom and low light obviously kill the image quality. It does yield beautiful JPEGs in good light, but the pictures look way better if you take them in DNG format and edit them to your liking, and use a better noise reduction software. The ONLY thing I dislike about this phone, the only one, is that the screen's contrast ratio isn't great. Blacks look grayish. The screen has lots of IPS glow. It's not AMOLED like the older Moto phones, but even by LCD standards, those blacks literally look grayish. It does have nice colors and gets bright, plus it's 1080p so it looks really sharp and clear. Doesn't look like a budget phone screen. Believe me! It looks very nice.

Camera was listed as a potential weak point for this phone, but we played around with multiple modes and settings and found it to take really nice images that NO one would be embarassed by. I recently purchased a Pixel 3a for myself and while the three years of software updates and truly superlative camera are strong selling points against the G7, when you look at the great build/look of the G7 as well as the expansive screen (for 100 LESS than the Pixel 3a!) I could see why someone might pick up the g7 instead. Can not go wrong. After playing with both the Pixel and the G7 for a few days, I honestly don't know how anyone can justify 800-1100 for a flagship phone.

It is somewhat awkwardly placed in the rear of the phone as other reviewers have mentioned. I find myself pressing the camera lens sometimes in an effort to unlock the phone. It is a pretty good way to get the camera lens dirty. The camera works well and although I am not terribly interested in much more than point and shoot photography... I am thinking about diving in and experimenting/learning all of the available features- I understand that this camera is very capable and I have admired the photos I have taken thus far. All in all, if I had it to do over (at the same price point) I would buy this phone again. I can’t think of a better review than that, folks. Enjoy!

I returned the second... Too bad, the price was right, it's an attractive package, but if folks can not understand you on the other end...
Camera. Have the phone a couple days ... So far love everything about it!
Good value. Like the phone but the camera quality should be better

Good phone, poor camera.. I love that it has lots of GByte room, and can even be expanded. I like the the screen size and the phone itself is attractive asthetically, but the camera sucks. Such a waste of a good looking phone. The camera itself and the photos it can take are one of the most important factors today with social media being one of the main uses for a phone. (I bet I'm not wrong) I'm disappointed in the camera, but other than that it good value for the money.

For this low cost $200, you'd be nuts to spend $800 or more. Son bought last year, great review from him, so I bought, couldn't be happier. Can't do the proximity scan payment method if you need that. Camera average. Crazy good battery life. Speaker can't go too loud so I use headphones for conference calls. I had a Samsung top end (older) and this is no downgrade. Allows SD card, Apple is so stupid about that.

That is going to do wonders on battery life. Also for gorilla glass, they sure didn't include that to protect the camera glass plate as I noticed a slight crack on it. I have no idea how it happened as I've been extra gentle with it even encasing it in protective case. Still despite those problems, the pros outweight the cons and worth checking out.

Outstanding phone and the price is right.. This phone is really good. I can not find any fault with it . The professional reviewers say the camera is weak and maybe it is. If so download the Pixel camera app and you have a B++ camera. The battery life is excellent and the response time is outstanding. Buy it.

06_rerank.text: The camera does need to be learned in order to avoid its weaknesses, since it's obviously not a flagship phone. Digital zoom and low light obviously kill the image quality. It does yield beautiful JPEGs in good light, but the pictures look way better if you take them in DNG format and edit them to your liking, and use a better noise reduction software. The ONLY thing I dislike about this phone, the only one, is that the screen's contrast ratio isn't great. Blacks look grayish. The screen has lots of IPS glow. It's not AMOLED like the older Moto phones, but even by LCD standards, those blacks literally look grayish. It does have nice colors and gets bright, plus it's 1080p so it looks really sharp and clear. Doesn't look like a budget phone screen. Believe me! It looks very nice.

Camera was listed as a potential weak point for this phone, but we played around with multiple modes and settings and found it to take really nice images that NO one would be embarassed by. I recently purchased a Pixel 3a for myself and while the three years of software updates and truly superlative camera are strong selling points against the G7, when you look at the great build/look of the G7 as well as the expansive screen (for 100 LESS than the Pixel 3a!) I could see why someone might pick up the g7 instead. Can not go wrong. After playing with both the Pixel and the G7 for a few days, I honestly don't know how anyone can justify 800-1100 for a flagship phone.
Camera not so good. Moto g4 plus has better camera.. Camera is not good. Rest is fine.
I'm not enough of a camera geek to compare cameras. Otherwise, the Moto G7 delivers a comparable user experience to the Samsung S10 for 1/3 - 1/2 the price.

I returned the second... Too bad, the price was right, it's an attractive package, but if folks can not understand you on the other end...

Outstanding phone and the price is right.. This phone is really good. I can not find any fault with it . The professional reviewers say the camera is weak and maybe it is. If so download the Pixel camera app and you have a B++ camera. The battery life is excellent and the response time is outstanding. Buy it.

CONS: *Battery life could be better. I use my phone heavily throughout the day for audio streaming and navigation, and have to charge it once or twice in a day. *For those who like to tinker under the hood, the Developer options are not readily available. *The fact that the battery is not replaceable by the user was the biggest obstacle I had to overcome in deciding to purchase this phone, but considering that's the direction the entire industry is going, whatcha going to do? I haven't used the camera much (and am not much of a photographer), but the snaps I have taken have been decent. BOTTOM LINE: If you're a shutterbug, you might want to look elsewhere, but if you're just looking for a phone with good performance that won't even cost you three bills, check out the Moto G7!

Like the features. Hate the poor network connection.. I bought this phone as an upgrade to my long used and very reliable Moto G2. As you can tell by my choice I don't required the latest high end features phone. I use my phone as a phone. Mainly calls with some texting thrown in and now the occasional look at my home security cameras which is the main reason I upgraded from the former G2. This phone constantly displays an "emergency calls only" message and to date I don't believe the signal strength indicator has risen above a third of it's range. My Moto G2 never had a network connection issue.

In good lighting the pictures look great, however shadows can stick out quite pathologically. Overall I am very satisfied with the product, keeping in mind that the weaknesses mentioned above are an acceptable sacrifice in quality for the cost of the phone. If you are trying to take near-professional quality images with a phone, this is not the product for you. Other than image acquisition and a mediocre (but acceptable) battery life, you likely won't notice any performance differences from higher-end phones.

Sound quality and signal strength are outstanding. Great price. Will soon buy another.. Great phone. Looks good, well priced, blazing fast processor. This replaces a Motorola G4. We had a very easy transition and love the speed of the new phone. Camera is fine, we use it for work and have no issues. Sound quality and signal strength are outstanding.

Not impressed. I bought this phone for the excellent camera reviews. The camera was terrible. Literally couldn’t take a clear picture no matter how still I held it. Text messages often didn’t deliver (and this was to other Android users - so not an iPhone issue). Also glitchy from the moment I bought it, with apps closing me out for no reason and freezing up. I returned the phone. Only gave it more than one star because I mean... it worked. Just didn’t work well.

It is somewhat awkwardly placed in the rear of the phone as other reviewers have mentioned. I find myself pressing the camera lens sometimes in an effort to unlock the phone. It is a pretty good way to get the camera lens dirty. The camera works well and although I am not terribly interested in much more than point and shoot photography... I am thinking about diving in and experimenting/learning all of the available features- I understand that this camera is very capable and I have admired the photos I have taken thus far. All in all, if I had it to do over (at the same price point) I would buy this phone again. I can’t think of a better review than that, folks. Enjoy!
camera not the best. the camera quality is not the best, which is disappointing, the focus takes forever
Camera fail. Camera sucks. Can't take casual pictures of my baby because they are all consistently come out blurry.

Does it all!. Can't beat the phone for the money .,. as good my grandkids expensive Samsung phones, at 25% of the coast. If it has a weakness, it's the camera, but then, I have an expensive 35mm for taking pictures
